newsitem.title: USA: Monterey sets reverse split, closes merger.
newsitem.headline: Monterey sets reverse split, closes merger.

text.p: Monterey Homes Corp said on Friday it set a one-for-three reverse stock split related to the recent merger with Monterey Homes Construction II Inc and Monterey Homes Arizona II Inc.
Monterey said its stockholders approved the merger on Dec. 23 and it was consummated on Dec. 31.

The transaction led to the termination of the company's tax status as a real estate investment trust although it is expected that the company's $58 million net operating loss carryforward will be available after the merger.
The company said it issued about 1.3 million shares of stock, bringing the total outstanding stock to about 4.5 million shares.
About 267,000 additional shares of the company's stock, as well as options to purchase about 334,000 shares at a price of $5.25 per share, were granted in the merger.
These rights and options, along with existing stock options, could lead to the issuance of about one million additional shares of Monterey stock, the company said.

Also related to the merger, the company said it changed its name from Homeplex Mortgage Investments Corp to Monterey Homes Corp, switching its New York Stock Exchange ticker symbol from "HPX" to "MTH".
William Cleverly and Steven Hilton, the prior owners of the purchased Monterey entities, will serve as chairman and president, respectively, and co-chief executives of the company.
Monterey said it will continue with the homebuilding operations of the Monterey entities in Arizona as its main line of business and will withdraw from the residual and real estate lending business.
